I went looking for an equivalent to the windows audio driver "loudness equalization" functionality and think I found something good https://github.com/the7erm/volume-adjuster

I'm using an old dual core laptop with xubuntu 15.04 mainly as a youtube machine (always have 100+ videos in my watch later playlist lately) and I'm running the audio out from the laptop into a hardware mixer and then into my main windows 7 machine's line input. Previously I had just been using the windows driver loudness equalization to take care of the problem of not all videos on youtube having proper/good audio levels but that has the unwanted side effect of boosting ALL SOUNDS in windows which isn't exactly ideal... it also created noticeable hiss on the line input.

This volume-adjuster will affect all sounds in linux but so far I have not been annoyed with it and it's better than having to mess with a volume control somewhere whenever you run into some video or audio that's too quiet.

I'm open to suggestions if anyone knows of a better or more interesting way of dealing with inconsistent audio levels of audio/video on linux, especially if it's something that could be localized to a web browser and not affect all sounds globally... it feels odd to just settle for the first thing I found like this.
